name: Kerala and the Tamil temple country: Kochi, Kuttanad, Munnar

cities.base: Fort Kochi, on the streets between the beachfront and Santa Cruz Basilica, or Mattancherry if you want the working town rather than the heritage one. You walk everywhere in Fort Kochi, the Mattancherr
cities.name: Kochi: Fort Kochi and Mattancherry

cities.base: Not Alappuzha town, which is traffic and a bus stand. Stay in a canal-side homestay or heritage house on the north canal or out at Punnamada, or better, 20 minutes south at Nedumudy or Chennamkary in
cities.name: Alappuzha and the Kuttanad backwaters

cities.base: Avoid Munnar town itself, which is a bazaar, a bus stand and a traffic jam with hotels. Stay in the estates 5 to 12 km out on the Chithirapuram, Pothamedu or Bison Valley side, where you step out of t
cities.name: Munnar and the Kannan Devan tea hills

cities.base: You do not sleep up here. Rajamalai is 13 km from Munnar, Kolukkumalai is a 4WD hour beyond Suryanelli, Marayoor and Chinnar are 40 to 60 km north on the Udumalpet road. All of it runs off a Munnar be
cities.name: The high range: Rajamalai, Kolukkumalai and Marayoor

cities.base: Inside the Masi streets, the concentric ring roads around the temple, so you can walk to the East gate at 05:30 and back at 22:00 after the night procession. North Masi and the Town Hall Road side hav
cities.name: Madurai

cities.base: Thanjavur near the palace and East Main Street, ten minutes by auto from the Big Temple and central for the Kumbakonam and Trichy loops. Kumbakonam is the alternative and puts you next to Darasuram an
cities.name: Thanjavur and the Chola country

places.name: The Chinese fishing nets, Vasco da Gama Square
places.note: Cantilevered dip nets, about a dozen of them, and maybe half still fish; the crews will wave you onto the platform and then ask 200 to 500 rupees for the privilege of hauling the rope.

places.name: St Francis Church
places.note: Built by the Portuguese around 1503 and the oldest European church in India; Vasco da Gama was buried here in 1524 and the empty slab is still marked. Free, 07:00 to 18:30, from 08:00 on Sunday, when the morning until about 10:30 is a service, not a visit.

places.name: Mattancherry Palace, the Dutch Palace
places.note: Closed Fridays, and the ticket is a few rupees, so the only cost is getting there. Built by the Portuguese, renovated by the Dutch, and the reason to go is the bedchamber murals: dense sixteenth and seventeenth century Kerala painting of the Ramayana with no free wall left.

places.name: Paradesi Synagogue
places.note: Shut Fridays and Saturdays and on Jewish holidays, and it breaks for lunch roughly 12:00 to 15:00, so the real window is two short slots. Built 1568, floored in hand painted Cantonese tiles no two of which match, and the congregation is now down to a handful of people.

places.name: Bazaar Road and the Jew Town spice godowns
places.note: The working end of Mattancherry: open warehouse doors with sacks of ginger, black pepper, turmeric and copra, men weighing by hand, and the smell changing every thirty metres. Most godowns are shut Sunday and half shut by 17:00.

places.name: Kerala Kathakali Centre
places.note: Makeup from 17:00 and the performance 18:00 to 19:00 for about 600 rupees; arrive for the makeup or do not bother, because watching the green paste go on is half of it. This is a one hour tourist cutdown of a form that runs all night.

places.name: Kayees Rahmathulla Cafe
places.note: Open since 1948 and the mutton biryani that Kochi argues about; short grain kaima rice, a boiled egg, and it is gone when it is gone, usually inside two hours of opening. Evening hours exist but the biryani is a lunch thing. Cash, shared tables, ten minutes walk from the synagogue.

places.name: A banana leaf sadya, Ernakulam side
places.note: The full vegetarian sadya is a lunch-only event at ordinary meals hotels: twenty odd items round a leaf, rice in the middle, parippu then sambar then rasam then buttermilk in that order, payasam at the end. Eat right hand only, fold the leaf towards you when done.
places.neighborhood: MG Road and Warriam Road, Ernakulam

places.name: Kashi Art Cafe
places.note: The Fort Kochi cafe that started the whole Fort Kochi cafe thing, in a Dutch house with a courtyard and a small gallery at the back. Good filter coffee and a decent breakfast, priced for foreigners, full of them. Fine for a slow first morning, not a discovery.

places.name: Fusion Bay
places.note: Small, plain, family run, and the karimeen pollichathu and the prawn moilee are better than anything on the seafront strip at half the price. They will show you the day's fish.

places.name: Dhe Puttu
places.note: Puttu, the steamed rice and coconut cylinder that is the Kerala breakfast, served fifteen ways with beef, kadala curry and fish. A local-crowd restaurant rather than a heritage one, twenty five minutes by auto from Fort Kochi, and the single easiest place to understand why Kerala eats what it eats.

places.name: Kumbalangi and the toddy shops
places.note: A fishing and crab farming village on the backwater edge where the Chinese nets still work for a living and the coconut climbers still tap toddy. A kallu shaap is an unsigned concrete room with a bench, fresh toddy in a steel jug, and the hottest fish curry in Kerala.
places.neighborhood: Kumbalangi, 15 km south of Fort Kochi

places.name: The overnight kettuvallam on Vembanad
places.note: Board around noon, cruise four hours, anchor by law before sunset, eat what the cook makes, sleep to a generator, move again at 07:00. Around 1,500 boats work this lake and the cheap ones at 6,000 rupees pump sewage and engine oil straight into water that villages still wash in.

places.name: The Kuttanad village canoe out of Nedumudy
places.note: A punted country canoe down canals a houseboat cannot enter, past paddy fields farmed two metres below sea level behind mud bunds, duck herds, coir soaking in the water and toddy tappers overhead. This is the backwaters people actually mean.

places.name: St Mary's Forane Church, Champakulam
places.note: A Syro-Malabar church the local tradition dates to AD 427, rebuilt many times, with a granite cross and Portuguese-era altarpieces inside; Kerala had Christians long before any European arrived. Free, open to anyone 06:00 to 18:00.

places.name: Ambalappuzha Sree Krishna Temple
places.note: Famous for its palpayasam, a milk and rice pudding cooked since the sixteenth century. Free, open 03:00 to 12:00 and 17:00 to 20:00; non-Hindus are not admitted past the outer gate, so check, and men who go in must be shirtless, women in a saree or mundu.

places.name: Mullackal Street bazaar
places.note: Alappuzha's own shopping street: gold shops, banana chip fryers working in coconut oil in the open, coir, cloth, and tea stalls. Most of it shuts Sunday. The Rajarajeswari temple halfway along does not admit non-Hindus, but the street around it is the point.

places.name: A Kuttanad kallu shaap
places.note: Toddy shops are licensed, numbered and almost never named on a board, so you find them by asking, not by searching a map; your canoe punter or houseboat cook knows which one is pouring fresh today.

places.name: Thaff Restaurant
places.note: Alappuzha's late night grill and biryani place, popular with locals rather than houseboat guests, and the kuzhi mandi and al faham show how much Gulf migration has rewritten Kerala's Muslim cooking. Loud, bright, fast. Good after a day on the water when everything else has closed.

places.name: Karimeen pollichathu on the Kumarakom road
places.note: Pearl spot fish, scored, packed with a chilli and shallot masala, wrapped in banana leaf and cooked on a tawa until the leaf chars. The small kitchens on the road in from Kottayam do it better and for a quarter of the price of the lakefront resorts.
places.neighborhood: Kumarakom lakefront, 30 km from Alappuzha by road

places.name: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary
places.note: Fourteen acres of mangrove and rubber on the lake edge, walked on raised paths. Migrants including Siberian stork, teal and pintail are there November to February and that is when it is worth the drive.

places.name: Pathiramanal island by shikara
places.note: A ten hectare island in the middle of the lake, reached by an hour of shikara, with a short birding trail and no shop and no shade to speak of. Take water.

places.name: Marari Beach
places.note: A long flat fishing beach with catamarans drawn up on it, a village behind and no promenade, which is the whole appeal after three days on brown water. The undertow is real and there are no lifeguards, so swim shallow. Sea jellies show up in some months and the fishermen will tell you which.

places.name: KDHP Tea Museum, Nallathanni Estate
places.note: Opened by Tata Tea in 2005 on the Nallathanni Estate: a working rolling, oxidation and CTC line, the original 1905 Pelton wheel, old rollers and dryers, and a film honest about the Tamil labour that built the district. Closed Mondays; the tasting at the end is short.
places.neighborhood: Nallathanni, 2 km north of Munnar town

places.name: The tea estate walk above Pothamedu
places.note: Estate roads and pluckers' paths through Kannan Devan tea, which is private land that nobody minds you walking on if you stay on the tracks and off the bushes. Go at 07:00 for the mist coming off the slopes and the pluckers going up with their shears.

places.name: Lockhart Gap
places.note: A road cut where the ridge drops into the Idukki valley and the cloud comes up through it in the afternoon. Free, no gate, no queue, and it is the one Munnar viewpoint that has not been fenced and ticketed. Best before 10:00 or you are looking at white.
places.neighborhood: On the Kochi road, 18 km south of Munnar

places.name: Mattupetty Dam and the Indo-Swiss dairy
places.note: A reservoir ringed by tea with a herd of crossbred cattle behind it, and the shore is genuinely good at eight in the morning. By eleven it is a car park, a row of corn roasters and men selling a twelve minute speedboat lap.

places.name: Echo Point
places.note: A lay-by where a coachload of people shout at a hillside and a smaller sound comes back. There is a ticket gate, a car park, pedal boats and a line of stalls. Drive through it to Top Station and spend the twenty minutes at Anayirankal instead.

places.name: Top Station
places.note: At 1,700 metres on the state line, looking down onto the Theni plains of Tamil Nadu, and it was the top of the old ropeway that took tea down to the plains before the road. Cloud usually fills the valley by 10:00, so this is a leave-at-06:30 trip or nothing.
places.neighborhood: Kerala and Tamil Nadu border, 32 km east of Munnar

places.name: Anayirankal reservoir
places.note: A bigger and much emptier reservoir than Mattupetty, ringed by tea and shola forest, with a dirt track along the shore you can walk for an hour. Elephants use the far bank and are occasionally on the near one at dusk, which is a reason to keep to the road and not camp. No gate and no fee.

places.name: CSI Christ Church, Munnar
places.note: A granite church consecrated in 1910, built by Scottish estate managers and workers, with stained glass, rosewood pews, the planters' memorial brasses and a cemetery of people who died young of blackwater fever. Free, fifteen minutes; go early for the mist. Sunday morning is a service.

places.name: Munnar old bazaar
places.note: Two streets of spice shops, tea merchants selling by weight from open sacks, hardware and vegetable stalls. Buy tea loose here rather than in the tourist shops on the Aluva road, where the same leaf is in a tin at four times the price. Cardamom and pepper are genuinely worth carrying home.

places.name: The bazaar chaikada at four o'clock
places.note: A tea stall with a glass case of parippu vada and banana fritters, chai pulled between two steel tumblers to cool and froth it. Late afternoon is when the estate buses come down and the place fills with pluckers. Twenty rupees for tea and a vada, and it is the most Kerala thing in Munnar.

places.name: Rapsy Restaurant
places.note: A plain bazaar restaurant that has been feeding Munnar for decades and is now in every guidebook, which has cost it nothing. Kerala parotta with beef fry, kothu parotta, and a bhelpuri that has no business being in a hill town and is the thing people queue for. Cash, packed at 20:00, turnover fast.

places.name: The evening thattukada carts
places.note: Roadside carts that set up at dusk: kallappam, egg roast, beef ularthiyathu, omelette and porotta cooked on a kerosene griddle while you stand. This is where Kerala actually eats at night, it costs about 200 rupees, and it is the one place in Munnar with no foreigner pricing. Nothing is mild.
places.neighborhood: Munnar bridge and the Aluva road junction

places.name: Eravikulam National Park at Rajamalai
places.note: Closed completely from 1 February to 31 March every year for Nilgiri tahr calving, which no weekly closed-day field can express and which ruins a February itinerary built around it.
places.neighborhood: Rajamalai gate, 13 km north of Munnar

places.name: Kolukkumalai sunrise and the orthodox tea factory
places.note: Leave Munnar around 04:30, transfer to a 4WD jeep at Suryanelli, and take an hour of rock track that no car will do to a ridge at 2,100 metres for sunrise over the Tamil Nadu plains. The factory at the top still runs a 1930s orthodox line by belt drive and will show you the whole process.
places.neighborhood: Above Suryanelli, on the Tamil Nadu side

places.name: Lakkam Waterfalls
places.note: A forest department pool below a short fall, with changing rooms and a ticket gate, and it is a reasonable twenty minutes on the way to Marayoor. It is a trickle by March and closed outright when the river runs high in the monsoon. Do not make a special trip.
places.neighborhood: Marayoor road, 22 km north of Munnar

places.name: The Muniyara dolmens, Marayoor
places.note: Iron Age burial chambers, four granite slabs and a capstone each, scattered across fields and a low hill; some are 3,000 years old and there are hundreds in the valley. Barely signed, occasionally a caretaker with a key and a ticket book, mostly just there.

places.name: The Marayoor sandalwood forest
places.note: The only natural sandalwood stand in Kerala, state owned down to individual numbered trees because of a poaching history that involved Veerappan. You cannot walk in alone; the forest office at Marayoor runs escorted entry and the rules change, so this is a turn-up-and-ask rather than a booking.

places.name: The Marayoor jaggery sheds
places.note: Marayoor sharkara has a geographical indication and is made in open sheds beside the cane fields: crushed juice boiled down in an iron pan over cane trash, poured into moulds, no chemicals. Growers will let you watch and will sell you a ball for a few rupees.

places.name: Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary and the Thoovanam trek
places.note: A rain shadow sanctuary of dry thorn and riverine forest, which is why it looks nothing like the rest of Kerala and why it is dry enough to have no leeches. The Thoovanam waterfall trek is about 8 km return with a compulsory tribal guide, booked at the Karimutty checkpost that morning.

places.name: Kanthalloor orchards
places.note: A valley that grows apples, plums, oranges, garlic and gooseberries at 1,600 metres, which nobody expects of Kerala, and smallholders will walk you round for a small fee. Fruit is on the trees roughly May to August, so outside that it is a quiet farming valley with good light and no fruit.

places.name: Vattavada vegetable villages
places.note: Terraced smallholdings at 2,000 metres growing carrots, beans, cabbage, strawberries and garlic for the Tamil Nadu markets, and the drive in from Top Station is the best hour of road in the district. Cold at dawn, genuinely cold, and the last stretch is single track with trucks on it.
places.neighborhood: Vattavada, near the Tamil Nadu border

places.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
places.note: It shuts from 12:30 to 16:00 and an itinerary that puts this after lunch loses the day.
places.neighborhood: Old city, inside the Masi streets

places.name: The Meenakshi night procession
places.note: Every night around 21:30 Sundareswarar is carried in a silver palanquin through the corridors to Meenakshi's bedchamber, with drums, nagaswaram and a crowd walking alongside. Free.

places.name: Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal
places.note: One courtyard and a dance hall of a 1636 palace that was four times this size until a later ruler carted the rest off to Tiruchirappalli. Twenty five metre columns, a domed hall with no beams, heavy Victorian restoration. Forty five minutes is plenty.

places.name: Puthu Mandapam
places.note: A 124-pillared Nayak hall from the 1630s with carved dynastic portraits on the columns, now occupied end to end by tailors, book stalls and tailoring machines. Nobody charges anything.
places.neighborhood: Directly east of the temple's east gopuram

places.name: Gandhi Memorial Museum
places.note: In Rani Mangammal's palace of about 1670, a museum since 1959, and it holds the blood-stained dhoti Gandhi wore when he was shot in 1948, plus a letter to Hitler and a Sevagram hut replica. Free; roughly 10:00 to 13:00 and 14:00 to 17:00, but sources disagree on the closed day, so check.

places.name: The Mattuthavani flower market at dawn
places.note: Madurai is the jasmine capital of India and this is where the malli comes in by the sack before dawn, gets weighed, argued over and sent to Chennai and the Gulf. Be there by 05:30.

places.name: Murugan Idli Shop
places.note: Started in Madurai in 1995 and now everywhere, but the Masi Street branches are the ones that matter. Idli on a banana leaf with four chutneys, sambar, and a spoon of poduthuval, refilled until you stop them. Breakfast costs about 150 rupees. Order the podi idli too.

places.name: Konar Kadai, Simmakkal
places.note: Kari dosai is a Madurai invention: minced mutton pressed into a dosa on the griddle with egg and onion, cut with a metal scraper, eaten standing.

places.name: Amma Mess
places.note: Madurai's non-vegetarian reputation in one room: mutton chukka, kari kola urundai, brain masala, kidney, and a mutton soup drunk at the start. Nothing here is for the squeamish and nothing is subtle. Cash, plastic chairs, and the queue outside is the review.

places.name: Jigarthanda on East Marret Street
places.note: Milk boiled down, nannari sarsaparilla syrup, almond gum, ice cream, served cold in a steel tumbler and named from the Urdu for cold heart. Two shops on the same street both claim to be the original and both are good; take whichever queue is shorter.

places.name: Kanadukathan and the Athangudi tile workshops
places.note: About 1h45 each way. Merchant mansions built on Burmese teak, Italian marble and Belgian glass by a banking caste that financed half of colonial Southeast Asia, most now empty and looked after by a caretaker who will show you round for 100 to 300 rupees.

places.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple, the Big Temple
places.note: Finished in 1010 under Rajaraja I, a 66 metre granite vimana. Free for all visitors, 06:00 to 20:30; the sanctum shuts roughly 12:30 to 16:00 but the ASI compound stays open, so you can still walk the courtyard and the Chola frescoes corridor at noon.

places.name: Thanjavur Maratha Palace and the bell tower
places.note: A half-ruined Nayak and Maratha complex where the Durbar Hall paintwork and the seven-storey Goodagopuram climb are the point, not the upkeep. Several separate ticket counters for the palace, the gallery, the library and the tower, each a few tens of rupees, each with its own attendant.

places.name: Thanjavur Art Gallery, the Chola bronzes
places.note: The best room of Chola bronzes anywhere, in a Nayak durbar hall with strip lighting and dusty labels, which is exactly why nobody is in it. Ninth to thirteenth century Natarajas, Parvatis and saints cast by the lost wax method that Swamimalai still uses.

places.name: Saraswathi Mahal Library Museum
places.note: One of the oldest working libraries in Asia, about 49,000 palm leaf and paper manuscripts assembled by the Maratha king Serfoji II, with a small public museum of a few dozen of them plus his medical atlases and physiognomy prints. Usually closed Wednesdays.

places.name: Airavatesvara Temple, Darasuram
places.note: The smallest and the best carved of the three Great Living Chola Temples, twelfth century under Rajaraja II, with a stone chariot front mandapam and a frieze of the 63 Nayanmar saints. The sanctum has a midday puja break of roughly 12:30 to 16:00 but the ASI enclosure is open through it. Free.

places.name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram
places.note: Rajendra I built a capital here after marching an army to the Ganges, and the temple is all that is left of it. Free, open 06:00 to 12:00 and 16:00 to 20:00, so not at midday; roughly 1h45 from Thanjavur, with a lion-mouthed well and a Nandi in the open.

places.name: The Swamimalai bronze foundries
places.note: Sthapathy families here still cast icons by the lost wax method the Cholas used, and the workshops will show you the beeswax model, the clay mould and the pour without any expectation that you buy.

places.name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam
places.note: Shut roughly 13:00 to 15:15 in the middle of the day. The largest working temple complex in the world, seven concentric walls and 21 gopurams with a 73 metre Rajagopuram finished in 1987, and the outer prakarams are a town with shops and houses inside the walls.

places.name: The Rockfort and Ucchi Pillayar Temple
places.note: 417 rock-cut steps, barefoot, up an 83 metre outcrop of some of the oldest rock on earth, with a seventh century Pallava cave temple partway and the Cauvery and Srirangam laid out at the top. Non-Hindus climb the rock and reach the summit terrace.

places.name: Degree coffee in Kumbakonam
places.note: Degree coffee means the first, undiluted decoction off the filter, with milk that has actually been boiled, and Kumbakonam is where south India argues it is done best. It comes in a tumbler and dabara and you pour it between the two to cool it, which is not a performance, it is how you drink it.

places.name: The unlimited banana leaf meals, Thanjavur
places.note: Lunch only, roughly 11:30 to 15:00, at any of the vegetarian meals hotels near the bus stand end of Gandhiji Road. A leaf, rice, four or five vegetables, sambar, rasam, kootu, buttermilk and an appalam, refilled until you fold the leaf. Around 150 rupees.

places.name: Santa Cruz Cathedral Basilica
places.note: The Portuguese built the first church here in 1505, the British knocked it down in 1806 and this Gothic one, frescoes and stained glass, was consecrated in 1905. Open 09:00 to 13:00 and 15:00 to 17:00; no entry fee found, so check the price.

places.name: Kerala Folklore Museum
places.note: Three floors of traditional Kerala architecture, crafts, folk art and antiques, with live Kathakali and martial arts shown and a handicraft shop. Open daily 09:00 to 18:00 and free going by one listing, so check the price.
places.neighborhood: Thevara, about 7 km from Fort Kochi

places.name: Dutch Cemetery, Fort Kochi
places.note: Dated 1724 on the gate pillar, 104 tombs and epitaphs, last burial 1913, and thought to be the oldest European cemetery in India. The CSI church keeps it locked most of the time and opens on request, so hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Indo-Portuguese Museum
places.note: Opened in 2000 for the church art of the Portuguese years: a 16th-century teak altarpiece from Our Lady of Hope, Vypeen, and a 17th-century silver processional cross from Santa Cruz. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Royale Park
places.note: The hotel restaurant on YMCA Road, about 1 km from the centre, with a bar alongside. Listed at 300 to 500 rupees for two, so 150 to 250 a head on an undated page, 07:00 to 22:30; hours vary, check.

places.name: Alappuzha Light House
places.note: The red and white tower finished in 1861 and lit in 1862, with a small maritime museum and the coast and backwaters from the top. 20 rupees for foreigners plus a camera fee; 09:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 17:00, closed Monday.

places.name: Revi Karunakaran Memorial Museum
places.note: A private family collection, mostly religious art: marble and crystal, a Kerala Room, a set of Tanjore paintings and a 250 ft mural. 200 rupees going by one visitor, so check the price; 09:00 to 17:00, closed Monday.
places.neighborhood: Alappuzha, about 1 km from the centre

places.name: International Coir Museum
places.note: How the coir industry that built Alappuzha works, from hand twisting to machines, with a short video. Visitors report 10 or 20 rupees plus 50 for phone photos, so check the price; 09:30 to 17:00, closed Monday.

places.name: Mullakkal Rajarajeswari Temple
places.note: About 500 years old with an open-roofed sanctum, the temple behind the bazaar, and it welcomes visitors of all religions. Open 05:00 to 12:00 and 17:00 to 20:00; no fee found, so check the price. The 41-day Mullakkal Chirappu festival is its big moment.

places.name: Saravana Bhavan, Munnar
places.note: A South Indian vegetarian place for thalis and dosas, 400 rupees for two on an undated listing, so about 200 a head. One site gives 09:00 to 23:30, another 07:30 to 21:30 and a point 650 m east, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Attukad Waterfalls
places.note: Several falls dropping through tea hills, open all day. Flow is low outside the monsoon, so in November it may be thin; one visitor says free, so check the price.
places.neighborhood: About 9 km by road from Munnar

places.name: Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam
places.note: A historic temple tank with a shrine in the middle you can only reach by boat, food stalls in the evening, and the teppam float festival in January or February. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Sree Ariya Bhavan
places.note: Pure vegetarian by the old bus stand: order the pot paratha, mud pot biryani, dosa or idiyappam. 300 to 500 rupees for two on an undated page, so 150 to 250 a head; 06:30 to 22:30 daily.
places.neighborhood: South Rampart, near the old bus stand

places.name: Madurai Uma Mess
places.note: A Madurai-style non-vegetarian mess, the change from all the temple-town vegetarian meals, about 3.7 km out. About 650 rupees for two on an undated page, so 325 a head; 07:00 to 23:00 daily.

places.name: Thillana
places.note: The Sangam Hotel restaurant, 06:30 to 23:00 daily. 200 to 400 rupees for two on an undated page, so 100 to 200 a head, though one review summary calls it dearer than the rest of Thanjavur.

places.name: Schwartz Church (CSI Christ Church)
places.note: Built in 1779 by Raja Serfoji for the Danish missionary C. F. Schwartz, a few minutes from the palace. The only listing gives Sunday service times, 07:00 to 11:00, so hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Hill Palace Museum, Tripunithura
places.note: Built in 1865 as the seat of the Maharajas of Cochin and a museum since 1986, the largest archaeological museum in Kerala. Do not miss the 1.75 kg jewelled crown and the porcelain gallery. 09:00 to 12:30 and 14:00 to 16:30, closed Monday, 50 rupees; go at 09:00.
places.neighborhood: Tripunithura, about 13 km east of Fort Kochi

places.name: St Andrew's Basilica, Arthunkal
places.note: A shore basilica founded in the 16th century, said to be rebuilt in 1584, and the largest St Sebastian shrine in the world per Kerala Tourism; see the carved teak Last Supper altar. 05:30 to 20:30, no fee listed, so check the price; the January feast brings crowds.
places.neighborhood: Arthunkal, about 18 km north of Alappuzha

places.name: Karumadikuttan Buddha
places.note: A black granite Buddha with its left half missing, dated anywhere from the 9th to the 14th century, found in the Karumady stream; Sir Robert Bristow built it a shrine in the 1930s. 08:00 to 18:00, fee unknown, so check the price; Ambalappuzha is 5 km away.
places.neighborhood: Karumadi, about 13 km southeast of Alappuzha

places.name: Thiruvampady Sree Krishna Swami Temple
places.note: A Kerala-style Krishna temple called the Dwarka of the South, dated to the 13th century on one listing, with two large temple ponds. Open 05:30 to 11:30 and 17:30 to 20:30; no fee stated, so check the price, the dress code and whether non-Hindus may go in.
places.neighborhood: Alappuzha, about 3 km southeast of the centre

places.name: Alappuzha Beach and the old pier
places.note: The town beach with the remains of the British-era ship pier, next to the lighthouse and the Revi museum, so do all three together. Free to walk on, parking is paid; come 17:00 to 19:00 for the sunset.
places.neighborhood: Alappuzha seafront, 2 km west of the centre

places.name: Pothamedu View Point
places.note: A lookout over a valley of tea, cardamom and coffee, free and open all day. It sits on the same hillside as the Pothamedu estate walk, so do them as one morning; sunrise or late afternoon is best.
places.neighborhood: Pothamedu, about 4 km from Munnar town

places.name: Ramaswamy Aiyar Headworks Dam
places.note: A check dam built in 1944 at the head of the Pallivasal hydro scheme, which one reviewer calls Kerala's first hydroelectric project, with walkways over the water. Open all day, no fee mentioned, so check the price; it is one stop in a chain with Mattupetty and Kundala.
places.neighborhood: Moolakadai, about 2 km northeast of Munnar

places.name: Koodal Azhagar Temple
places.note: A Vishnu temple, one of the 108 Divya Desams, named in the Sangam works Paripadal and Silappadikaram, Pandya in origin with Nayak additions and a five-tier gopuram. Free to enter, about 20 rupees for the upper levels; 04:00 to 12:00 and 16:00 to 20:00, so go in the morning.
places.neighborhood: Central Madurai, 1.5 km west of Meenakshi

places.name: Samanar Hills, Keelakuyilkudi
places.note: Jain rock-cut caves, stone beds and inscriptions from the 1st century CE onward and a carving of Mahavira, with a 30 minute marked climb to the top. Hours vary, check, and the fee is unknown, so check the price; go early before the rock heats up.
places.neighborhood: Keelakuyilkudi, about 8 km west of Madurai

places.name: Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple
places.note: A rock-cut hill shrine to Murugan, 6th century on one listing and the first of his six Arupadai Veedu abodes, with frescoes and views over the city. 05:00 to 13:00 and 16:00 to 21:15; a special darshan ticket exists, price unknown, so check the price.
places.neighborhood: Thiruparankundram, about 9 km southwest of Madurai

places.name: Kallazhagar Temple, Alagar Kovil
places.note: Vishnu as Kallazhagar, inside the walls of two forts over about 100 acres; at the Chithirai festival in April or May the deity goes down to the Vaigai. 06:00 to 12:30 and 15:30 to 19:30, darshan free, a fast ticket is 10 or 15 rupees.
places.neighborhood: Alagar Hills, about 19 km northeast of Madurai

outings.why: Chinese nets, St Francis, the Dutch Palace murals, the synagogue and then two kilometres of open spice godowns along Bazaar Road, on foot the whole way. The hard part is the day you pick: the palace is shut Friday, the synagogue is shut Fri
outings.name: The Fort Kochi to Mattancherry walk, Bazaar Road end to end
outings.season: All year. Never on a Friday.
outings.fallback: Stop at the synagogue, take the auto back, and spend the afternoon at the Kathakali makeup instead.

outings.why: Arrive at 17:00 for the hour of face painting, stay for the hour of performance. What you are seeing is a one hour edit of a form that traditionally runs from dusk to dawn, with the story explained in English first. Real temple Kathakali ha
outings.name: Kathakali at the Kerala Kathakali Centre, from the makeup
outings.season: Nightly all year. Temple Kathakali December to April.
outings.fallback: The Kalaripayattu at 19:15 in the same hall, which is 400 rupees and better theatre than the abridged Kathakali.

outings.why: North of Kochi is the older layer: two restored synagogues of a Jewish community that predates the Portuguese, a Jewish cemetery at Chendamangalam with a 1269 tombstone, and the Cheraman Juma Masjid at Kodungallur, which claims to be the fi
outings.name: The Muziris run: Paravur synagogue, Chendamangalam and the Cheraman mosque
outings.fallback: Hill Palace Museum at Tripunithura, the largest archaeological museum in Kerala, also shut Mondays, half a day.

outings.why: A punted canoe into canals no houseboat fits down, through paddy farmed below sea level, coir retting, duck herds and toddy palms. It is the backwaters without the diesel. Go at 07:00; by 10:00 it is hot and the light is flat, and the punte
outings.name: The Kuttanad canoe out of Nedumudy
outings.season: All year. Fields are flooded June to September and green and
outings.fallback: An hour of shikara on Punnamada from the jetty, about 800 rupees, which shows you the lake and none of the villages.

outings.why: Fourteen acres of mangrove on the east shore of Vembanad, walked on raised paths at first light. November to February brings the migrants and makes it worth the early start; the rest of the year it is egrets and darters and a pleasant hour.
outings.name: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary at six thirty
outings.season: Worth it November to February; open all year
outings.fallback: Pathiramanal island by shikara, three hours, which gets you out onto the open lake instead.

outings.why: Book a slot online, drive 13 km, take the forest bus up and walk a 3 km tarred loop through shola grassland where Nilgiri tahr graze a few metres off the path. It is the single best chance in India of seeing a rare ungulate without a guide
outings.name: Rajamalai and the Eravikulam tahr
outings.season: Open all year except 1 February to 31 March
outings.fallback: The tea estate walk from Pothamedu up to the Lockhart Gap road, free, three hours, and empty.

outings.why: Out of Munnar at 04:30, swap into a 4WD at Suryanelli, an hour of rock track to a 2,100 metre ridge on the Tamil Nadu border for sunrise, then the 1930s orthodox tea factory at the top, which still runs on belt drives. The track is the hard
outings.name: The Kolukkumalai sunrise jeep
outings.season: All year, clearest December to March
outings.fallback: Top Station at 07:00 by ordinary car, one hour of driving, the same plains view from 400 metres lower.

outings.why: North over the ridge into the rain shadow: Iron Age dolmens in the fields, the state sandalwood forest, the jaggery sheds, then the Thoovanam waterfall trek in Chinnar with a compulsory tribal guide. Dry thorn forest, no leeches, and nothin
outings.name: Marayoor and Chinnar in one day
outings.season: All year. Jaggery sheds run December to April, Thoovanam is
outings.fallback: Marayoor dolmens and the jaggery sheds only, back by lunch, about four hours.

outings.why: Through the East gate before the heat, into the Potramarai tank court and the thousand pillar hall while the granite is still cool and the flower sellers are setting up. Non-Hindus go everywhere except the two gold sanctums. Phones and came
outings.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple at five thirty
outings.season: All year. Chithirai festival in April and May adds a million
outings.fallback: Puthu Mandapam and the Nayak palace, both a short walk, if the temple is shut for a procession.

outings.why: Around 21:30 every night Sundareswarar is carried in a silver palanquin to Meenakshi's bedchamber with drums and nagaswaram, and anyone standing in the corridor can watch the whole thing go past. Free, forty minutes, and almost no foreign v
outings.name: The Meenakshi night procession
outings.fallback: Kari dosai at Konar Kadai in Simmakkal, which does not get going until 21:00 anyway.

outings.why: Ninety kilometres east, about 1h45 each way, into a district of enormous merchant houses built on Burmese teak and Belgian glass and now mostly empty, opened by a caretaker for a hundred rupees. The Athangudi handmade tile workshops are the
outings.name: The Chettinad mansion loop: Kanadukathan and Athangudi
outings.season: All year. Hot and flat April to June.
outings.fallback: Azhagar Kovil and the Pazhamudircholai hill temple, 21 km north of Madurai, half a day.

outings.why: Brihadeeswarar at 06:15, when the granite is cool enough to walk barefoot and the vimana catches the first sun. Unlike Meenakshi, non-Hindus go all the way to the lingam, and the ASI compound stays open through the midday temple closure if
outings.name: The Big Temple at first light
outings.fallback: The palace art gallery and the Saraswathi Mahal library, ten minutes away, if it rains.

outings.why: The other two Great Living Chola Temples plus the bronze workshops between them. Darasuram is the best carved of the three and is usually empty; Gangaikonda Cholapuram is 1h45 north on poor road and is all that survives of Rajendra's capita
outings.name: Darasuram, Gangaikonda Cholapuram and the Swamimalai foundries
outings.fallback: Darasuram and Swamimalai only, five hours, skipping the northern leg.

outings.why: An hour west to the largest working temple complex on earth, seven walls deep with a town living inside them, then 417 barefoot steps up the Rockfort for the view back over it. Srirangam shuts roughly 13:00 to 15:15, the Rockfort stone is u
outings.name: Srirangam and the Rockfort
outings.fallback: Srirangam alone in the morning and back to Thanjavur for the bronzes, five hours.

destination.name: Kerala and the Tamil temple country: Kochi, Kuttanad, Munnar
destination.pitch: Twelve days buys you the best food in India, a week of water and tea hills that ask nothing of you, and then three Chola temples and a Nayak one across the ghats that are the equal of anything in the Golden Triangle with a tenth of the coac
destination.caveat: The southwest monsoon shuts the coast from June to early September and the northeast monsoon floods Tamil Nadu in October and November, so the trip really only works December to March, and even then the big temples close from about 12:30 to 16:00 every single day. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Kochi is the only real city on the route and it is a small one; Madurai is a temple with a town round it and Thanjavur is a country town with a wonder in it.
because.food: Sadya on a leaf, toddy shop fish curry with kudampuli, Mattancherry biryani that sells out by two, kari dosai at midnight in Madurai, and degree coffee in Kumbakonam, all of it under five dollars.
because.nature: Shola grassland with wild tahr at Rajamalai, a rain shadow sanctuary at Chinnar with no leeches in it, and two thousand kilometres of canal you travel by punted canoe rather than on a path.
because.culture: Meenakshi at dawn and its night procession, three Chola temples including the 1010 Big Temple, Kathakali from the makeup up, a 1568 synagogue and a church that held Vasco da Gama's body.
because.adventure: A 4WD track to Kolukkumalai at 04:30 and a guided trek to Thoovanam, and that is honestly the extent of it; this is not a trip you come to for the adrenaline.
because.relaxation: A night anchored on Vembanad, an empty fishing beach at Mararikulam, and estate mornings in Munnar where the only thing on the schedule is walking downhill through tea before breakfast.
because.exploration: Five distinct places in twelve days, none of which resembles the next: a Portuguese and Jewish port, a delta farmed below sea level, tea at two thousand metres, and a Tamil temple city that has never stopped working.
